paper_metadata.title: Development of new γ′-strengthened Co-based superalloys with low mass density, high solvus temperature and high temperature strength

evidence.quote: Development of new γ′-strengthened Co-based superalloys with low mass density, high solvus temperature and high temperature strength

The present work reports new γ/γ′ quaternary Co-Al-Ta-Cr based superalloys with low mass densities in the range of 8.3 to 8.5 gm/cm3, solvus temperatures up to 1128 °C and good mechanical properties even at high temperatures.

Alloy ingots weighing 100 grams of nominal composition (all in at. %) Co-xNi-10Al-5Cr-2Ta-yTi (x = 0, 10, 20, 30, y = 0 and x = 30, y = 2, 4) were prepared using constituent elements of 4N purity in vacuum arc melting unit under argon inert atmosphere using a tungsten electrode and a water cooled copper hearth. The alloys were melted 8-10 times with flipping of the button after each melting cycle to ensure homogeneity throughout the ingot.
The prepared ingots were cast into rods (Φ-3mm, L-80mm) using vacuum suction casting unit under argon atmosphere using a water-cooled split copper mold.
The cast samples were solutionized at 1200 °C for 20 hours in a vacuum tube furnace (10^-5 mbar) followed by water quenching.
These were aged at 800 °C for 0 to 50 h for the alloy compositions with x = 0, 10 and 20 and at 900 °C for 0 to 1000 h for rest of the alloys followed by water quenching.

An activation of multiple slip systems with temperature assisted cross slip of superpartial dislocations from high antiphase boundary (APB) energy (111) octahedral plane to low energy cubic (100) plane led to formation of KW (Kear-Wilsdorf) lock at elevated temperature. These locks further obstruct the motion of coming dislocation and thereby provides addition strengthening.
